Maryland Online Casino Legalization Fails for a Fourth Straight Year

Published September 21, 2026 · 4 min read · By the OddsLighthouse Editorial Team

Maryland lawmakers once again failed to advance legislation that would legalize regulated online casino gambling in the state, marking the fourth consecutive year the effort has stalled, according to reporting this week from PlayUSA and BettingNews. State Sen. Ron Watson had reintroduced two measures this session — a proposed constitutional amendment that would send the question to voters as a ballot referendum, and a separate bill laying out a regulatory framework for licensed online casinos — but the Senate version, SB 761, drew an unfavorable report from the Senate Budget and Taxation Committee and was withdrawn by Watson on March 13, 2026. A companion measure from Del. Vanessa Atterbeary in the House also failed to reach the floor before the session's crossover deadline.

Why Maryland needs a constitutional amendment

Unlike states that can authorize online casino gaming through ordinary legislation, Maryland's constitution requires voter approval via referendum before commercial gambling can expand, which is why Watson's bill was structured as a proposed constitutional amendment rather than a standalone regulatory bill. That requirement adds an extra hurdle beyond the usual legislative process: even if a bill clears the General Assembly, the question would still need to go before Maryland voters before any online casino could legally launch. Opposition from the state's existing land-based casino operators, who have argued that legal online casinos would cannibalize retail casino revenue without generating enough new tax revenue to offset the loss, has been a recurring factor in each year's failure.

Why it matters to Maryland bettors and players

Maryland continues to offer retail casinos and legal online sports betting, but residents still have no regulated online casino option, leaving the state on the sidelines of a market that has now grown to eight states. Had this session's legislation succeeded, Maryland would have become the ninth state to regulate online casino gaming. Sen. Watson has indicated he plans to bring the proposal back when the General Assembly reconvenes in January 2027, meaning the earliest Maryland residents could plausibly see a regulated online casino market is likely still years away, pending both legislative passage and a successful statewide referendum.
